simple.meaning: רָאמָה (râʼmâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “something high in value , i.e. perhaps coral.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רָאמָה (H7215) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 28:18, with occurrences in Job, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָאמָה (H7215) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רָאמָה (H7215) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רָאמָה (râʼmâh) / H7215 is traced through Job 28:18, Ezekiel 27:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: something high in value , i.e. perhaps coral
definitions.full: H7215. ramoth I. רָאמוֺת noun [feminine plural] usually corals (so Ki; black corals Thes ( מְּנִינִים = red corals ); compare Arabic , sea-shell , We Heid. 2. 163 ); — as costly Job 28:18 , as merchandise, רָאמֹת Ezek 27:16 ; — חָכְמוֺת לֶאֱוִיל רָאמוֺת Prov 24:7 , reading and sense dubious, see Toy. רָֽאֲמָה , II. רָאמַת רָאמוֺת, see רום , II. רמה . above

occurrences.englishText: No mention will be made of coral or of crystal.
